learning.title: Check the boundary rails before ruling on DB shape - the rails are codified policy that outranks the ruling
learning.body:
#520 (2026-11-17): the PM ruled a CHECK constraint (XOR over content/blob_id) was "shape, not policy" and belonged in the DB. Two things the ruling missed: (1) the PostgreSQL boundary rail REFUSES CHECK constraints in new migrations (0166 has none for that reason) - the rail is codified policy, written for migration recoverability, and it outranks an ad-hoc structure/policy ruling; (2) retention purges versions by setting content to null, so "no home" is a legitimate THIRD state - exactly-one was wrong, at-most-one is right.
Rule: any ruling that touches a new migration checks the boundary rails first (they live as tests that refuse migration shapes - run the rail or read the list). "Structure vs policy" is an analysis, not an override; where the rail disagrees, the rail wins and the invariant moves to the write path, pinned by a test that fails when the write path violates it (learning 123 form: fails by assertion on the named property).
Corollary: name the LEGITIMATE EMPTY STATES before ruling on column constraints - "purged", "expired", "abandoned" are each a state a row can be in, and a constraint that forbids one of them will be refused by the suite that tests it (here, the retention tests refused to insert their purged rows). The existing suite is a better oracle for schema shape than first principles.
